0.content:
Sara's devotion to the Raiden Shogun is the centre of her life. She believes the Archon granted her a Vision in the instant she fell from a cliff as a child, saving her life, so everything she has exists by the Shogun's grace. The Shogun is her "will, her future, her strength" and also a kind of repose for someone with few friends. She vows to help manifest Eternity even if she never sees it, and to return her Vision to the Shogun "without hesitation and with no regrets" when the time comes. She admits she does not always grasp the Shogun's words ("Abandon mortal ties, strive for an unchanging Eternity") but trusts her decision.

The Shogun's voice-over praises Sara as a loyal, righteous subject and accomplished warrior "worthy to be called a hero", and says that with such an heir the Kujou Clan's future is assured. After the Decree's repeal Sara says the Shogun has not erred, only chosen a different road to Eternity. She does not know whether the Shogun has found peace, but will follow her "however perilous the road ahead".

Thunder, to her, "speaks the will of the Almighty Shogun". She went on the Shogun's orders to observe the Warrior's Spirit exhibition match (3.4, limited). What she knows of Ei and the puppet is never shown; Yae Miko says Sara pesters her with questions about Ei.

1.comment: Kujou Sara: Kujou Takayuki and the Kujou Clan
1.content:
Takayuki, head of the Kujou Clan and Tenryou Commissioner, adopted the nameless tengu girl because her Vision marked her as heaven-sent, named her Sara and trained her to serve the Shogun and secure the clan's position. Sara is grateful, but knows he never looked at her the way he looks at his son Kamaji, and she feels lonely seeing her soldiers with their families. As a child she was coldly rebuked while the soldiers who played with her were severely punished. Kamaji, his younger son, is on friendly terms with her.

In 2.1 she learned Takayuki had dealt with the Fatui, kept the Decree going in exchange for their backing, and hid the war's cost from the Shogun. She forced her way into his presence, heard him admit it all, and called him a hypocrite who taught loyalty only so her loyalty would stop at the clan. The Shogun was displeased by the deception. Takayuki lost his position and, per a later notice, is under house arrest awaiting punishment. Kamaji became acting clan head; Sara and the eldest son, Masahito, continue to lead the army.

Documents from a Yashiori Island exploration objective (Tatarigami Investigation Expedition) record that Takayuki threatened to replace Masahito with "his adoptive sister" when Masahito reported the Tatarigami's effects. Masahito says Sara told him about the ceasefire and the Traveler, though he does not trust the peace. In 2026 Kamaji urged Sara to invite friends over on her days off.

2.comment: Kujou Sara: The Vision Hunt Decree
2.content:
Sara was the Decree's main enforcer. She believed Visions in misaligned hands would destabilise Inazuma, and she led troops to confiscate them, while ordering that civilians must not be harmed or exploited. Her officers' brutality toward detainees troubled her more than anything, and she could not stamp it out. She doubted the Decree privately but chose obedience. After its repeal she says she trampled on people's ambitions and must atone. She asked the Traveler to tell her of the ambitions echoing from the Visions embedded in the Statue of the Omnipresent God.

As the Shogun's servant she was allowed to keep her own Vision. Her victims include Kazuha's friend and Arataki Itto, whose Geo Vision she took.

3.content:
Sara first met the Traveler as Inazuma's most wanted criminal, branded an enemy of Eternity. At the Resistance front in 2.0 she offered Gorou a respite in exchange for handing them over, then proposed a fight of honour; the Traveler won bout after bout, and Kokomi's reinforcements forced her to retreat. In 2.1 the Traveler and Yae Miko brought her the proof of Takayuki's treachery, and the Traveler fought beside her through the Tenryou guards. She calls them "a good example of achieving concord through conflict" and says she never imagined fighting alongside them.

She regards them as an "unstable factor" in the Shogun's Eternity, though not a threat, and still watches them. She has never seen them as a subordinate and picked them as her conversation "training partner". Her birthday letters invite them to spar, tend her bow, plan a day off and, in 2026, simply drop by "as an old friend would".

4.comment: Kujou Sara: Sara's Vision and the Fall
4.content: Before she had a name, Sara lived in a quiet mountain forest overrun by monsters. Young and with damaged wings, she fought them alone and was hurled off a cliff. As she fell she cried out that she had always believed she could protect the place with her strength. At dawn passers-by found an unconscious girl, apparently unharmed, by the roadside, holding a glowing Vision. They took her to the Tenryou Commission. Sara believes the Archon's gaze in that instant saved her life, and that fighting for the Shogun is her truest calling.

5.comment: Kujou Sara: Kazuha and the Duel Before the Throne
5.content: Under the Decree, Kazuha's friend challenged the Vision hunters to a duel before the throne, where the loser faces divine punishment and the victor gets a second chance. Sara fought him and won. As the sentence fell, Kazuha arrived, snatched his dying friend's Vision and fled Inazuma. Kazuha accepts her victory as proof of her strength but cannot forgive her for using it as "an oppressor's lackey". Later he concedes she has ideals of her own, and wonders whether the Kujou family can flourish again.

6.content:
Sara beat Itto and confiscated his Geo Vision during the Decree. He made more fuss than anyone she had arrested, though he admitted defeat "like a man". He now demands a sumo rematch, calls her "Kujou Tengu" and threatens "Kujou Chicken" if she keeps refusing, and left a challenge on the Uyuu Restaurant board. Sara bristles at his name and refuses to discuss the rematch. Canon never shows how it went.

During the limited-time 2.7 Drumalong event, a notice from Sara warned the public about an event "of unknown purpose" hosted by "itinerant youths who call themselves the Arataki Gang". She grudgingly credits Kuki Shinobu with keeping the gang from disturbing the peace.

7.comment: Kujou Sara: Sangonomiya Kokomi and the Peace Talks
7.content:
Kokomi, Watatsumi's Divine Priestess and strategist, repeatedly bloodied Sara's forces; before they had met, Sara already credited the "grand strategist" with keeping the resistance alive. After the war they negotiated the peace (Kokomi's Story Quest). Sara proposed lifting fishing restrictions with taxes, a Yashiro Commission trade council, and the return of Watatsumi's forces to Tenryou command. Kokomi exposed two Tenryou soldiers who had been contacted by Signora's remnants. Sara interrogated them on the spot, apologised for her negligence and vowed to hunt the Fatui down. She dropped the military demand until the Commission was in order. She concluded she would rather settle differences at a table than on the battlefield.

Kokomi calls her an opponent "that cannot be taken lightly" and the person in Inazuma City who most adores the Shogun. Sara wonders whether to adopt Kokomi's directive cards for the Shogun's Army. In 2025 she visited Watatsumi Island off duty at Kokomi's invitation, went pearl diving, received a coral bracelet, and did not know how to thank children who gave her Loach Pearls.

8.content: Gorou commanded the Resistance troops against Sara. They met "countless times in battle", with wins on both sides. Gorou calls her perhaps the most honourable officer in the Shogun's Army and once wished she could be free of the Shogunate's grip. Sara says Gorou is to Kokomi what she is to the Shogun, is glad of an admirable foe, and is pleased to hear he is a fifth-born son.

9.comment: Kujou Sara: Yae Miko and the Proof of Guilt
9.content: To weaken the Tenryou Commission, Yae Miko invited Sara to the shrine and promised proof of Takayuki's betrayal if she returned alone in three days. The Traveler, with the Kamisato household's help, stole Takayuki's falsified report and his Fatui correspondence. Reading them, Sara was enraged that soldiers' deaths and civilians' hardship went unmentioned, and stormed off to confront him. She respects the Guuji because the Shogun trusts her, though Yae's actions leave her with "many questions". She warns that if Yae ever defies the Shogun's will, she apologises in advance. Yae calls her "not the sharpest tengu in the forest", but credits her bluntness.

10.content: Learning from Takayuki that the Harbinger Signora was at Tenshukaku as a Snezhnayan diplomat, Sara rushed to confront her and was found lying unconscious before the throne. The Shogun stopped Signora, declaring that the right to punish Inazumans was hers alone. The Traveler then won a duel before the throne against Signora, who was executed by the Shogun's Musou no Hitotachi. Later, hearing that Tenryou soldiers had been approached by "HER subordinates", Sara swore to hunt them down, every last one.

11.content: Heizou is a Tenryou Commission doushin and Sara's colleague. She has "few positive words" for him: he follows his own schemes and vanishes without explanation, and only his results keep her from bringing him into line ("He is such a headache"). He calls her the most serious person in the Commission and wishes she would give everyone some breathing room. At Lantern Rite (6.3, limited) she trusted that, with Heizou around, no thief would touch the lanterns she planned to hang at Headquarters.

12.comment: Kujou Sara: Statues of Her Excellency
12.content: The lacquerware "Statue of Her Excellency, the Almighty Narukami Ogosho, God of Thunder" is the most popular Shogun merchandise in Inazuma. Sara was first in line on launch day, which became a minor scandal she never answered. She keeps five in display cases in a shrine she prepared herself and cleans them whenever she is home, hiring artisans when she cannot. She calls the statue Inazuma's most distinctive item, "No, it is not a blade."

13.content: Shinobu calls Sara "Madam Kujou" and a friend from before she joined the Arataki Gang; their spars are too close to call. Sara regrets that someone of Shinobu's talent joined the gang, but admits her presence has kept idlers from disturbing the public and eased the Commission's burden.

14.comment: Kujou Sara: Inazuma's Views of Sara
14.content:
- Thoma warns that she holds great power, is not open to persuasion, and that smiling won't help; she would hire him in a heartbeat.
- Ayaka has had disputes with her but calls her a loyal servant of Inazuma; Sara would like to play Go with Ayaka but fears she would not fit into the lively Kamisato household.
- Ayato calls her Takayuki's most formidable weapon, one the old man can no longer wield.
- Yoimiya: Sara will cause her no trouble as long as no fireworks go off in her camp; she admires them but warns herself against their fleeting beauty.
- Kirara watches her from afar, curious about her wings and shed feathers. Sara has noticed a gaze in the shadows and wishes the nekomata would just come up to her.
- Yumemizuki Mizuki treats Tenryou soldiers Sara sends her; Sara's own mindscape is "cold, hard metal", which Mizuki respects and wonders at.

15.comment: Kujou Sara: The Bake-Danuki of the Mountains
15.content: Sara keeps the tengu habit of going to the mountains, knows them well and has seen many creatures absent from human tales; to her, benign and evil ones differ only in form. When thefts plagued the city, she caught the bake-danuki culprits, reclaimed the loot and gave them a "final warning". They never stole again. Afterwards she left long-keeping fruit at their den whenever she trained nearby, as consolation for those who had turned from an unrighteous path.

16.content: In a limited-time 2.2 event, the Traveler found Sara at Tenryou Commission Headquarters with too few men to deal with a Domain that had opened near Araumi and was spewing monsters. She gratefully accepted help from the Traveler and the Liyue musician Xinyan, promising in return to sort out Xinyan's expiring permit.

17.comment: Kujou Sara: Hues of the Violet Garden (2.6 event)
17.content: During the limited-time 2.6 Irodori Festival event, Sara caught Venti in a crate of Dandelion Wine and held him as a suspect in a theft and as a possible stowaway. She cleared the theft charge on the Traveler's reasoning, released him only when a Yashiro Commission invitation letter turned up, and advised him to stay at the International Trade Association. She later arrested the editor Onodera as a suspected book thief, posting two extra squads in case he ran, and was ready to leave once testimony cleared him.

18.content: In a limited-time 3.4 event, Sara observed the Warrior's Spirit swordfighting exhibition on the Shogun's orders. She congratulated the Traveler and Kamisato Ayaka on their win, said she had learned from their technique, conveyed the Shogun's recognition and left to report at Tenshukaku.

19.comment: Kujou Sara: Lantern Rite in Liyue (6.3 event)
19.content: During the limited-time 2026 Lantern Rite (A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon, 6.3), Sara visited Liyue and booked a souvenir photograph through Pingxi; the Traveler turned out to be the photographer. She planned to buy Xiao Lanterns for the entrance of the Tenryou Commission and was impressed that the Millelith kept strict discipline amid the festivities. She promised to keep the photo carefully among her personal effects.
